title: Attention Block
hints: Fix the bottom row of a candidate rectangle. For each column, how tall is the run of allowed cells ending at that row?
That turns every row into a histogram of heights. The question becomes: what is the largest rectangle inside one histogram, and how do you do it for all R rows without rebuilding from scratch?

Update heights row by row (reset to 0 on a blocked cell). For one histogram keep a stack of columns with increasing heights; when a shorter column arrives, pop taller ones and price the rectangle each could have formed, whose width is bounded by the new top of the stack and the current column. Sweep a sentinel 0 at the end. Total O(R*C).

wrong.square_only.cpp: finds the largest square instead of the largest rectangle
wrong.row_runs_only.cpp: only considers rectangles of height 1 (the longest run in a single row) and full-height columns
wrong.tle_column_scan.cpp: for every bottom-right cell scans upward tracking the minimum width, O(R*R*C) (fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: an R x C attention mask (up to 1500 x 1500) of allowed (1) and blocked (0) cells; find the area of the largest rectangle made only of allowed cells. Which plan fits?
options: Try every pair of corners and check the rectangle with prefix sums
Find the largest square with a DP on the neighbours and report its area
Turn each row into a histogram of consecutive allowed heights and find the largest rectangle in each histogram with a monotonic stack
Sort the rows by how many allowed cells they have and merge the biggest ones
strategy.why: Trying all corner pairs is O(R^2 C^2), about 5*10^12 at the limit. A rectangle need not be a square, so the square DP undercounts. Sorting rows ignores that the allowed cells must line up in the same columns. Heights per column plus a monotonic stack price every maximal rectangle once, O(R*C).
